pool.text: The Portuguese planned subsidiary forts in Montevideo to stop frequent Spanish insurrections.
Captain Manuel Henriques de Noronha reached Montevideo with soldiers, guns, and colonists.
Portuguese forces withdrew from Montevideo Bay after signing an agreement with Spaniards.
Bruno Mauricio de Zabala officially mentions the foundation date of the city.
Complete independence from Buenos Aires as a real city was finally reached.
A beacon replaced the observation post at the location of the fortress.
Palacio Salvo was completed after being designed by architect Mario Palanti.
Every match during the first FIFA World Cup was hosted here.
Juan Manuel Blanes Museum was established in the Palladian villa.
Jose Belloni's bronze monument La Carreta was installed near Estadio Centenario.
Fun Fun Bar was established as an important place for tango.
The Obelisk of Montevideo was built on Artigas Boulevard.
The Graf Spee retreated to Montevideo's port following the naval battle.
The Tarancos residence passed to the city to eventually house a museum.
The Planetarium of Montevideo was built within the premises of the zoological garden.
The Punta Brava Lighthouse became electric.
Art suffered when the military junta took over power in Uruguay.
The dictatorship proposed a new constitution which was rejected by referendum.
Montevideo Shopping became the first shopping mall in the Southern Cone.
A bicycle sharing system called Movete was launched in Montevideo.
